match.reason: No point in the bank covers comparing financial ratios over time, against similar businesses and against targets; benchmarking and monitoring performance are related ideas but are not about interpreting ratios.

draft.title: Comparing ratios
card: A single ratio tells you little on its own. A net profit ratio of 8% could be good or poor, depending on what it is compared with.
Over time
compare this year's ratio with the business's past years. This shows whether the business is improving or getting worse.
With similar businesses
compare with a business of the same type and similar size, or with an industry average. Different industries can have very different normal ratios.
With targets
compare with the goals the business set itself. This shows whether it did what it planned to do.
draft.remember: A ratio gains meaning only when it is set beside something else.

a.q: Why is it not enough for a business to calculate its current ratio once and look at that figure alone?
opts: The figure has little meaning without a comparison
The figure is always wrong unless it is audited
The figure only matters to the owners of the business
The figure cannot change from one year to the next
a.why: A single figure does not show whether the result is good, poor, improving or worsening. It needs a comparison, such as past years or similar businesses. Saying it is always wrong is tempting, but the issue is meaning, not accuracy.
a.clue: What can you say about a number with nothing to set it beside?

b.q: Priya owns a bakery in Orange. Her net profit ratio rose from 6% to 9% in three years. Her main aim is to learn whether she is doing better than other bakeries of her size. Which comparison does she need?
opts: Her ratio against the average for similar bakeries
Her ratio this year against her ratio three years ago
Her ratio against the target she set last January
Her ratio against a large supermarket chain's ratio
b.why: She wants to know how she does against other bakeries, so she needs a comparison with similar businesses. Her rise over three years is a comparison over time, which shows her own trend but not how she stands against others. A large supermarket chain is not similar in type or size.
b.clue: Her trend already shows change. Her question is about other businesses.

a.best: The figure has little meaning without a comparison

b.best: Her ratio against the average for similar bakeries

problems.detail: The remember line says a ratio gains meaning 'only' when set beside something else, which is a little stronger than the card's 'tells you little on its own'. Consider 'A ratio means much more when it is set beside something else.'
